title: Shakshuka
subtitle: North African eggs poached in spiced tomato sauce
excerpt: Eggs poached directly in a vibrant, deeply spiced tomato and pepper sauce fragrant with cumin, paprika, and harissa. One pan, twenty minutes, extraordinarily satisfying.

recipe.sourceNotes: Shakshuka (sometimes spelled shakshouka) is a dish of eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce that is widely eaten across North Africa and the Middle East. Its origins are contested between Tunisia, where the name comes from Maghrebi Arabic, and other North African and Levantine cuisines. The dish became extremely popular in Israel, where it was introduced by Jewish immigrants from North Africa, and is now considered a staple of Israeli cuisine. The sauce is built on a base of onion, red pepper, tomato, and aromatic spices including cumin and paprika, typically sharpened with harissa or chilli. Eggs are cracked directly into the sauce and cooked to order. Shakshuka is traditionally served with bread for scooping.

content.text: The eggs should be cooked until the whites are just set but the yolks are still runny; cover the pan for the last 2 minutes to help the whites set from steam while the yolks stay liquid. The sauce can be made up to two days ahead and refrigerated; add the eggs and finish just before serving.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan. Cook the onion and pepper over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, tomato puree, and harissa. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tinned tomatoes, crushing them roughly. Season with salt. Simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce has thickened slightly. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

Make wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each well. Cover the pan and cook for 3 to 5 minutes until the whites are just set and the yolks are still runny. Scatter with feta and coriander. Serve directly from the pan with flatbread or crusty bread.
